draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Shravanabelagola! Up on Vindhyagiri stands the Gommateshwara statue of Bahubali, 17 m tall and carved from a single block of granite over a thousand years ago.
draft.hungryLine: This is a small temple town and my notes don't list eateries, so keep meals simple and carry water for the climb.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Akkana Basadi is a 4 min walk, Chandragiri Hill about 7 min, and the Gommateshwara statue on Vindhyagiri about 8 min.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Take the quieter western stairs up Vindhyagiri, they're just as good as the main steps and far more peaceful.
moodReplies.surprise-me: The base of the Gommateshwara statue has inscriptions in Kannada and Tamil, plus the oldest evidence of written Marathi, from 981 AD.

spots.name: Gommateshwara statue
spots.detail: 8 min walk · The giant Bahubali statue on Vindhyagiri

spots.name: Chandragiri Hill
spots.detail: 7 min walk · Older Jain temples, and fewer crowds

spots.name: Akkana Basadi
spots.detail: 4 min walk · A Hoysala-era temple built by a devout lady

legends.title: Bahubali's choice
legends.body: Jain legend says Bahubali could easily have beaten his older brother Bharatha in a duel, but stopped and gave up his kingdom for meditation. The statue shows him standing still so long that creepers wind up his legs and arms.

legends.title: An emperor's last days
legends.body: Chandragupta Maurya is said to have died on Chandragiri hill in 298 BCE after becoming a Jain monk. A small basadi on the hill carries his name.

tips.title: Wear socks for the climb.
tips.body: The hill must be climbed barefoot, and in summer the rock gets hot, so two pairs of socks help.

tips.title: Give Chandragiri its own day.
tips.body: Many people only see Vindhyagiri, but Chandragiri is just as interesting, minus the statue.

story.title: Chandragupta's hill
story.body: Chandragupta Maurya is said to have died on Chandragiri after taking up the life of a Jain monk.

story.title: A statue for a mother
story.body: Chavundaraya, a minister and commander of the Ganga kings, had the Gommateshwara statue carved and erected it for his mother.

story.title: The elder sister's temple
story.body: Achiyakka, wife of a Hoysala minister, built Akkana Basadi in 1181 during the rule of Veera Ballala II.

story.title: A triple shrine
story.body: The Odegal Basadi on Vindhyagiri, held up by stone props, is the only triple shrine here and dates to the 14th century.

story.title: The great anointing
story.body: Every 12 years the statue is bathed with water, milk, saffron, flowers and more in the Mahamasthakabhisheka. The last one was in 2018.
